title: A brief per track, and questions that matter: what Home understood for each kind of help, and a Not sure that keeps it
request: Complete the Home plan package by package; H4 gives the analysis, preparation, reporting, business and advice tracks a brief of their own, asks only what matters, and fixes the defect H1 found: an I'm not sure that erased an outcome Home had understood.
spec: Package H4 of Phase H: each track has its brief with status, source and quote; a field is asked only when it is unknown and has no safe default, within a per-track budget (prediction 4 as today, analysis 2, preparation 3, reporting 4, business 3, advice 1); every question has a Not sure button that records the default; options come from the table's columns. Done when: on H1 dev, median questions per request at most 3 and no brief field is wrong that the rules left unknown; the prediction track keeps today's fields, order and budget.
plan: Write each track's fields with why, a default where one is safe, and where its options come from.
Write keyword rules per field in English and Persian that claim a field only when its words are there, each value with the person's words that say it as the quote.
Drop a field that names a snake_case column the table does not have, and say so when asking.
Ask the one field with no safe default, within the track's budget; answers to brief questions are recorded by code.
Make a Not sure keep what Home understood, on every track, the prediction's outcome included; give every question a Not sure button.
Show the brief on Home; measure on H1 dev and compare every prediction case with HOME-003.

decisions.decision: A field's value and its quote are kept apart.
decisions.why: The value can be one word ('region'); the quote is the person's words around it ('per region'), which pass the product's quote rule.

decisions.decision: Only a field with no safe default is asked.
decisions.why: A default is shown and editable; asking for it adds a question that changes nothing about the route or the answer.

decisions.decision: A Not sure is never recorded as the answer.
decisions.why: H1 measured that it replaced an outcome Home had understood; a non-answer must leave what is known and take only the default.

decisions.decision: A missing column is checked only for snake_case names, and only against a table that is there.
decisions.why: A column name is the one kind of word that can be checked; ordinary words are not columns.

change: New dclab_rnd/draft/brief.py (TRACK_FIELDS, BUDGET, RULES, extract, refresh, options, next_field). lang.py: NOT_SURE and not_sure in both languages. chat.py: ask() with a track, open_track refreshes the brief and asks its one question, brief answers taken by code, a Not sure keeps the plan's fields, move_to closes other tracks' questions, data_ready and replan refresh the brief, the model's context holds it. Home: the What I understood list and a Not sure button on every question. tests/test_home_brief.py (13 tests); test_home_eval and test_home_intent updated. HOME-004_dev.

findings.defect: An I'm not sure replaced the outcome Home had understood (found by H1).
findings.scenario: On H1 dev, three requests lost a field Home had read from them when the runner answered the column question I'm not sure.
findings.cause: take_answer recorded any reply as the field's value.
findings.fix: A not-sure reply is never a value: what was understood stays, the field is not asked again, and a track field with a default takes it.

findings.defect: After a Not sure to the outcome question, Home never asked for the outcome again.
findings.scenario: A vague request, Not sure to the outcome, then a table with a churned column: no outcome question, the summary said the outcome was still open.
findings.cause: The field counted as asked, and the column question needs a known outcome.
findings.fix: When a table offers outcome columns and no outcome is known, a not-sure outcome question is set aside so the outcome is asked again with the columns.

findings.defect: With a model, a Not sure still replaced the outcome.
findings.scenario: The model answered the pending question by recording target = 'Not sure'.
findings.cause: Only the no-model path knew about not-sure replies.
findings.fix: A not-sure reply to any open question is taken by code before the model sees it.

findings.defect: Real answers that began unsure were thrown away.
findings.scenario: 'Not sure, but probably whether they cancel within 30 days' recorded nothing.
findings.cause: The not-sure rule matched the start of a reply.
findings.fix: Only a whole short reply is a not-sure.

findings.defect: Any reply to a brief question became the field's value, and Home then said nothing.
findings.scenario: 'Actually I'd rather predict which customers will ask for a refund' was stored as the measure, with no reply.
findings.cause: Code took every reply as the answer and only asked the next question.
findings.fix: A reply that reads strongly as another kind of help moves there; a recorded answer, a not-sure and a missing column are each said back.

findings.defect: The missing-column rule erased preparation steps and defaults.
findings.scenario: 'Join orders_2024 and customers on id and remove duplicate rows' with a table lost its inputs and steps, and Home asked for steps the person had given.
findings.cause: Every field was checked against column names, and a missing column gave unknown instead of the default.
findings.fix: Only fields whose values are columns are checked; a missing column falls back to the default.

findings.defect: The missing column was named against the wrong field, or not at all.
findings.scenario: '…by sales_channel' asked the measure question with 'I can't find sales_channel'; a dropped breakdown with a default was never mentioned.
findings.cause: Missing columns were kept as one list for the whole brief.
findings.fix: Missing columns are kept per field: a field with no default names it in its question, a field with a default says it once.

findings.defect: Field rules claimed fields from words that do not say them.
findings.scenario: 'Show the breakdown by sales region' gave the measure 'breakdown'; 'by the end of the year' gave the breakdown 'end'; 'track how our app is doing' filled the numbers; 'Combine orders.csv…' cut the step at '.csv'.
findings.cause: The rules were written from the dev requests.
findings.fix: Each of these words is excluded or the rule is reordered; file names keep their dots.

findings.defect: An answer naming a missing column was accepted.
findings.scenario: Typing 'lifetime_spend' as the report's numbers, with no such column, was stored.
findings.cause: Only the sentence was checked against the table.
findings.fix: Answers to column fields are checked too, and the person is told.

measurements.name: Home on the H1 dev requests, rules alone, after H4 (HOME-004)
measurements.gate: home_gate_v1: track accuracy with the model at least 0.85 and with the rules alone at least 0.70; no new wrong field, bad quote, uncited number, identifier shown or unconfirmed row drop; median questions at most 3; every trap passes
measurements.result: Fields right 64, wrong 0, missed 14, abstained 17 (HOME-003: right 3). Fields lost to I'm not sure 0 (HOME-003: 3). Median questions 0. Traps 5 of 6 (missing_column now passes; silent_drop needs the data-preparation package). Track 1.0; quotes, uncited numbers and rows shown 0. Every dev prediction case asks the same number of questions as in HOME-003 and now keeps its outcome.
measurements.against_gate: rules_track_accuracy 1.0 against at least 0.70: met; no new wrong field (0 wrong): met; quote_invalid 0 and uncited 0 against 0: met; median questions 0 against at most 3: met; traps 5 of 6 against all: not met; the gate is read with the model, which has not run.
limits: The field rules were written from the dev requests, so 64 right on dev is an upper bound; the single sealed run at the end of Phase H is the honest test.
The H1 runner answers every question Not sure, so the measurement shows what Home reads from the request, not how it uses answers.

outcome: Home now holds and shows what a person said for every kind of help, takes and marks a default where one is safe, asks only what it cannot assume, and a Not sure never erases what it understood.
lessons: Measure the non-answer: the runner's I'm not sure found the worst defect in Home's question loop, and the fix is in every track, not only the one where it was seen.
A new button is a new path: the Not sure button on every question made an old corner (an outcome answered not sure before the data) easy to reach, and the review found it.
risks: Keyword rules for free-form fields can take a nearby word for the field; every rule claims a field only with its own words, and the review's sentences are the check.
